utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Although I have a list of some close to 20 items for a court agenda, I limit myself to only one at this very moment. On the 19th of February, the Defence informed the Chamber and the Prosecution, by e-mail, that it would not be able to schedule the testimony of a witness before today's date, the 1st of March. For that reason, the Chamber decided to cancel the hearing of Monday, the 29th of February. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Oien, if that's the way I have to pronounce your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oien, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Oien, before you give evidence in this court yes, apparently I -- do you receive interpretation in the English language at a volume audible for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please say again, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you receive interpretation in the English language and -- yes, and at such a volume that you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the texts of which is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Oien. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Oien, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find Mr. Ivetic to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would first ask that you state your full name for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: My full name is Per Oivind Oien.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have you ever testified before the Tribunal or any other court?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I am a retired officer of the Norwegian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you retire from the Norwegian Army?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you retired, what rank did you have in the Norwegian Army?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With a was your last assigned post within the Norwegian Army prior to retirement?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I was a chief of plans in the regional command in Trondelag. That's the Regional Command Trondelag, also named in Norwegian DKT, District Command Trondelag.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you ever deployed to the former Yugoslavia in any capacity?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I was deployed to the former Yugoslavia from October 1994 until October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What organisation were you deployed as a member of?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I was a United Nations Military Observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What had been your posting within the Norwegian armed forces prior to being sent to the former Yugoslavia as part of the UNMO?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Prior to my last posting was since 1987, I was a chief of staff at my home regiment in north Trondelag.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what was your rank at the time that you were deployed to the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where in the former Yugoslavia were you deployed and located while a member of the UN Military Observers?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: After arriving in Zagreb in October 1994, and a week's introduction course, I was deployed to the Sector North which was in the Slunj-Topusko area first as a team leader and then as a liaison officer in the Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you eventually get deployed to any other areas in the former Yugoslavia as part of UNMO mission?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: In March, early March I believe it was in 1995, I was deployed to Sarajevo as the SMO, Senior Military Observer, in Sector Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, as the SMO, Senior Military Observer, in Sector Sarajevo, what were your formal duties and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I was responsible for leading the team of UNMOs in Sarajevo consisting of approximately 100 officers from 16, 17 different nations and to make sure that the UNMOs could do their job properly, that -- to facilitate their work, to make sure that they followed the rules that was decided, gave them support in the team, support both morally and, of course, logistically. I also had -- my task was to be liaising with especially the chief of police inside Sarajevo and -- the liaison officer on the BSA side in Lukavica, yes, that means that liaising on that level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just have clarified. Where you said that one of your taskings was to sure that the UNMOs could do their job properly, I take it, you intended to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, who were your immediate superiors within the UNMO structure at the time?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: My immediate superior at the time was a Pak -- a colonel from Pakistan and name I have forgotten who was attached to the UNMOs. He was in the BiH command in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there any other superior within the UNMO structure higher than yourself?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: And then, of course, there was the CMO, a Brazilian general in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, on occasions where there was to be an UNMO investigation in Sarajevo in relation to a shelling incident who, according to the ordinary course and practice of the UNMOs, would be in charge of that investigation?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: In charge of the investigation would be the team leader of the teams assigned to the task. If there was shelling in the AOR, they were asked to do the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now when I ask you about something we have in evidence from a witness, Colonel Richard Mole and that's from transcript 4322 of this trial, he talked about a position that he called the chief operations officer for all UNMO groups that would analyse data sent in by the UNMO groups. Is that a position that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you repeat the number so that we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Transcript page 4322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned the Pakistani colonel whose name you had forgotten in the BiH command. What was his role?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I -- well, he was my superior and he was the superior of all the UNMOs in BiH area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would the person you identified as a Pakistani colonel in BiH command, would he in that position, ever take commend over investigations of shelling incidents in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No, not in my opinion. I don't remember any -- anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, if we can focus on the post in UN headquarters in Zagreb, which you saw at the time was a general from Brazil, what would the role of that officer be as to investigations being undertaken by UNMO in Sector Sarajevo of shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus with you on a particular investigation and if we could take a look together at P797 and I do have a hard copy to make it easier for you, which if I could have the usher's assistance to, first, show the same to opposing counsel and then to provide the witness. And then in e-court -- well, I'll wait. And we have, of course, the first page of a coded cable from Lieutenant-Colonel JRJ Baxter to UN PF Zagreb and several other acronyms and it talks about a mortar incident of 28 August 1995 and if we turn to page 2 in both versions, we could see a little better which incident is at issue. On page 2, we see that we are talking about a mortar attack on the Markale market in Sarajevo on 28th August 1995. First of all, sir, are you familiar with this incident referred to in this document known as the Markale market shelling that occurred in August 1995 in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were any of your subordinate UNMOs from Sector Sarajevo involved in that investigation of that incident?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, they were. There was a team from -- that was responsible in that area led by Dutch Lieutenant-Colonel Konings, or something, I think his name was. And they conducted an investigation of that shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And to whom did the UNMOs in Sarajevo doing the investigation of that shelling, to whom did they send their reporting of the investigation of that shelling?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: To the UNMO headquarters. That's my headquarters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you, sir, personally involved in any aspect of the investigation following the Markale market shelling in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Not involved in the investigation. I visited the scene, let's say, 20 minutes after the incident, just to make sure that my men on the ground had good working conditions, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we have looked at the first two pages of this document and you have a hard copy in front of you so you may do so again, if you wish to look at the first page. Do you believe that you had occasion to see this particular document, the first two pages of which are the transmission sheets, did you see this document any time in 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I'm quite sure I didn't see this document. The first time I saw when was you sent it to me in September last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we can look here on page 2 of the document, dated 8th September, 1995, again, with the heading Lieutenant-Colonel JRJ Baxter, MA to Commander HQ, UNPROFOR, we see here, at item b, he says that: "We have the investigation by UNMO patrol from Sector Sarajevo. The full UNMO report is at Annex B." And so I'd like to turn with you to page 9 in both languages of this document which should be Annex B that he refers to and I think we have it on the screen and hopefully ... you have it in front of you in hard copy. And the first question I'd like that ask you is does this that we have on our screens now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, can you indicate where we find the indication Annex B. In the -- in the B/C/S, it looks like it. Dodatak A.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. The -- even in the -- in the English original, we have what looks like A scratched off and then we have annex and looks like a B that's cut off at the far right above the number 5 so that's the ... that's the -- on the English original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the previous page, we did see Annex B. The way it's following, it's Annex B, the words you quoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, first, the question I have for you is this document that we have before us, does it resemble a standard UNMO daily situation report?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we see here at the top approximately one-fourth down, we see two names and we see first that this was prepared by a Major Mizan, DO. Who was this individual?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Major Mizan was the duty officer on duty at that time in my operation room in the headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is that what the designation DO stands for?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: DO is the duty officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then we have released by and then your name followed by the initials SMO. What precisely was your role in drafting and issuing this report?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Normally, the report was issued by the -- my operation officer, but I was present in the headquarter at that time, so I approved the report and that's why my name is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what precisely would have been the role of Major Mizan, the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Major Mizan the duty officer here, he got all the informations on the observations from the teams, and he then made this report as we can see it here. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to look at this entire report to prepare for today?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And ... you've mentioned the -- lieutenant-colonel from -- team leader -- I think it was Colonel Konings you said. Was there anyone else within the UNMO Sarajevo structure that was involved in the investigation of the Markale market shelling in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were two of his team members involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did either of your superiors, that is to say, the Brazilian general who was the chief UNMO in Zagreb or the Pakistani colonel who was the officer in Sarajevo -- at the BiH command did -- did they have any role in the investigation and reporting as to the August 1995 Markale market shelling?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 13 in the English and page 14 in the Serbian and we see at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for clarity, we are -- and rightly so, Mr. Ivetic, we're referring to e-court pages because the page 13 in e-court is -- finds a page 5 typewritten page number and a 9 in a circle handwritten. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And... okay. That's at the top, yeah. And looking at the bottom half of the document, we see here it says: "The following" ... "The following is a repeat and update of the interim daily sitrep passed on to selected addresses at 28, 1415 B August concerning a significant firing incident which occurred earlier today." 5

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Ivetic. Could you please slow down and first I take that you wanted to say selected not addresses but addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You are correct. You are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Having looked at the report, do you know which significant firing is at issue?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know which significant fire incident is at issue here?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: This is the shelling at the marketplace, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And having looked at the following pages through page 14 and what is written here, does it comport with your recollection as to what the UNMO report that you released as to the Markale market shelling of August 1995 says?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we can turn to page 14 in English in e-court and page 15 in Serbian in e-court, and if we could focus on the middle of the page, we see the notation here in parentheses: "(Full incident report will follow this DSR when team has reported has concluded investigation and reported to this HQ)." And, first of all, sir, could you tell us what the acronym DSR refers to?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Daily situation report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it says here: "When the team has reported has concluded investigation and reported to the [sic] HQ." Which HQ is this referring?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: "This HQ" is the UNMO HQ, my HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we turn to the next page in both languages, we appear to have a second document, again starting at the top at page 1. And this appears to be in a similar format of an UNMO daily sitrep, and it says: "UNMO Sector HQ daily sitrep update 28 August 1995, 1720 to 2359 hours and appears to be dated 29th August 1995. First of all, sir, what was the custom and practice as to when sitreps would be sent on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly if we sent one or two sitreps every day. Definitely we were to send one sitrep at the end of the day. And, as I remember, when a special incident happened, we should send one during or as fast as we could during the day. Maybe - I'm not sure - we sent two sitreps, but definitely one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this one that we have in front of us prepared by Captain Ihab DO, which we now know is duty officer. And it says, released by captain Ford OPSO. Who were both of these persons in relation to the UNMO organisation in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Captain Ihab was the duty officer working in my OPS. Captain Ford was my operation officer at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall if you would have seen this particular report in 1995 at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I saw it in 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we could turn to page 17 in English in e-court and page 19 in the Serbian in e-court. And we see here, under B, that UNMO team Sedrenik was tasked to investigate the impacts in the general area of the marketplace and then we have several points that are in relation to that. I would like to focus on the second bullet point which says: "One projectile was fired from 170 Mag DEG, killed 33 people (UNMO confirmed 31 killed) and wounded 79 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. "(64 names provided by min of health) in a busy shopping marketplace and the following one that says: "The bearing in combination with estimated angle of impact could not provide exact MOR position or an accurate origin of fire since it was not known with which charge the MOR projectiles were fired. Therefore range of firing position along bearing line could not be determined." Could you tell us, sir, if this text is consist with your recollection of the results of the UNMO investigation that was completed of the Markale marketplace shelling in 1995.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next page in the English and stay on the same page in the B/C/S, at the bottom of the B/C/S and at the top third of the English version, we see the comment: "UNMOs are unable to confirm which WF fired the rounds." First of all, sir, do you have a recollection as to what WF is implying?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, it's the warring factions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is this comment also consist with your recollection of the UNMO investigations of the Markale marketplace shelling in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 20 in e-court in the English and page 22 in e-court in the Serbo-Croat, we come to a page that says "end of sitrep update," did you have a chance to look at the entirety of this report yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Just for clarity, I believe Mr. Ivetic is referring to the sitrep report which is contained within a greater report. So we have clarity on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do have you occasion to review the entire UNMO daily sitrep released by Captain Ford --

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you believe that the UNMO sitrep released by Captain Ford and the report that you released on the same day, which we looked at earlier, taken together are the full UNMO report as Colonel Baxter indicated on the second page of this batch of documents we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Probably it is, yes. But to be clear, at the time the first report went out, the investigation and the details about that was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of course. And now after the daily situation report by Captain Ford was sent at midnight on 28 August 1995 were you or UNMO Sector Sarajevo HQ asked to undertake anything in relation to investigating the Markale marketplace shelling?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall your UNMO Sarajevo HQ ever changing or departing from the findings or conclusions voiced in this report released by Captain Ford?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would now like to take look at a document with you. A moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P00012 in e-court. And I also have a hard copy for the witness that, with the assistance of the usher, I'd like to show first to opposing counsel and then to the witness. The one I'm getting is different than the one that I have in hard copy. Is this also 65 ter number 10240?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the second page of the same. Now, this is a different document than I was looking for. Let's call up 65 ter number 11190, which should also be, I think, Exhibit P2608. Okay. This is more what I was looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have a document before us. Do you think you need a hard copy of this or ...

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Probably not. It's on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then, looking at this, across the top it says UNMO HQ daily sitrep and in the date it looks like this is dated 30th of August, 1995. First of all, sir, which UNMO HQ is issuing this daily sitrep?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: This is the UNMO HQ in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And had there been any changes in the conclusions reached by UNMO Sarajevo as to the Markale market investigation, would you expect to find a record of any changes in the sitreps issued by the UNMO HQ in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Well, I have to -- you have to proceed so I can look at what they say about Sector Sarajevo. You have to go on in pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Let's me ask a different question. Did you have occasion to review the ... the UNMO HQ Zagreb sitreps for the 29th of August through the 2nd of September, 1995 yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No. I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to ... I'll move on now. I'll get back to this after I find the page number of that particular one so as to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you: Had there been any change in the findings and conclusions of the UNMO investigation as to the Markale marketplace shelling of August 1995, what would have been the standard operating procedure for the same? Would -- according to the UNMO procedure. Would a written record be made or not?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure if I understand your question. Could you please try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Had there been any change in the conclusions reached by the UNMO investigation, would there be a written record of the same?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And why is that?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Well -- I mean, the facts were on the ground and we reported what we saw and that was the facts and no one can change that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now did any UNMO units, outside of your own Sector Sarajevo, undertake any investigations in addition to those conducted by your UNMOs as to the Markale marketplace shelling of August 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now if we could turn back to Exhibit P797, which I think you still have the hard copy of. That's the Baxter packet which also contains the two UNMO sitreps. And if we could look at page 6 in e-court in English and it's also page 6 in e-court in the Serbo-Croatian. And we have before us a document dated 6th of September, 1995, signed by a Lieutenant-Colonel Mougey SOO. First of all, sir, can you identify for us what organisational part of the United Nations forces was the engineer cell that appears to be the source of this document? Was it a part of UNMO?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No, it was not. It was a part of the French forces in Sector Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And looking at this document, prior to your preparations for this trial, do you recall if you'd ever seen this document in 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now the author of this document says here, in relation to the tail fin, he says: "After the discovery and examination of the tail-fin it appeared that it was a 120-millimetre mortar that had been fired ... 2850 (the angle from the point of impact towards the firing point). "This munition is of Serb manufacture, being unmarked and unpainted with a brushed steel finish, which matches current Bosno-Serb war design." And now earlier we had looked at the UNMO daily situation reports, and if we could turn to page 14 of this same document in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, when you read you left out one word.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When you referred to 2850 mils, the word before that, was "from." I think this is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is. Every word is important. And if we could turn to page 14 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And up at the top of the English, the third bullet point from the top, and in the B/C/S it will be the third bullet point -- second bullet point from the bottom and it says here: "One mortar tail was recovered with batch marking No MK/M74/KB93070." Were you aware of any differences in the description of the tail-fin as stated by -- between these two different accounts, one the Lieutenant-Colonel Mougey document and the UNMO sitrep report we're looking at now, were you aware of any difference in the description off the tail-fin in 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No. As I said earlier I don't recall seeing the document issued by the French engineers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what was the basis of the information in the UNMO daily situation report that the tail-fin was marked with batch markings?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the basis was, of course, that they found the tail-fin and it was marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you if you remember any oral briefings or meetings that you would have personally participated in where the topic of the Markale shelling from August 1995 was discussed in the BH command prior to the commencement of NATO air-strikes against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and I'm quite sure of this, that I never took part in any discussions --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt there are multiple components in that question, if we could break it up a little bit, maybe just so we have a little bit clearer record. Meetings about Markale shelling with whom, when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you please take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, let's start at the most basic level. Do you remember any oral briefings or meetings that you personally participated in where the results of the Markale market investigation by the UNMOs was the topic?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. And as I said, I'm quite sure I did not take part in any discussion, meeting, or conference about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you familiar with a General Cornelis Nicolai from The Netherlands who was a part of the BH command, specifically the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I read these documents, yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at our trial at transcript page 10655 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before he is actually allowed to testify about this, it's a little unclear on the record what documents he is -- what his basis of knowledge is that he is about to go into. He is referring to some documents being shown to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, to the extent it would cause any concerns, would you lay a foundation for any information you elicit from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I was about to do. But, first, before I do that, I will address the other question of Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you had looked at some documents I believe yesterday. What documents are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I looked at the documents you gave me about different aspects around this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what type of document was that? Who was it from?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't recall who it was from, but I believe that was the document -- the last document you're referring to is a statement by this Dutch general who I believe was the Chief of Staff in the BH command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification. Yes, indeed, you were asked whether you were familiar with this Dutch commander, you said you read these documents yesterday. Could you answer the question that was put to you? Prior to reading the documents yesterday, were you familiar with this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never met the men, I never knew about him, and I was not familiar with this man until yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are not familiar with this man, you are only familiar with the documents you read yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at our trial, General Nicolai testified at transcript page 10665 to 10666 as follows: "Q. General, I'd like to clear up the issue of what actually you reviewed, what reports you reviewed since we have been using general terms and I think that the Chamber might be under the misapprehension that you actually reviewed the written reports for Markale. I think the easiest way to do this is to look at your 2006 statement, which is 65 ter 1D00917, and it's page 5 of the same in English, page 9 in the B/C/S, and it's paragraph 3 I'd like to go over with you. And if you can follow along with me, sir, I'll read into the record the following portion." And then we read from the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads relevant portion, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Pardon me, relevant portion. "I have read documents numbered R001-5992 to R001-6013, which pertain to the shelling of Markale market on 28 August 1995. I had not read all those reports before, and I based my opinion stated in paragraph 14 of my statement on my recollection of a verbal briefing by the chief UNMO in Sarajevo. I seem to recall that briefing was addressed to our small circle of senior staff that included General Smith, myself, the heads of G3 and G2 and the respective military assistants. G2 was the head of the intelligence branch, and the G3 was head of the operations branch. I think we discussed the preliminary results of the investigation, and I further believe that the direction of fire was discussed because not only the distance matters. I have checked my notes of that day, and I have recorded that I was briefed that the shell came from the south, south-west. I also have recorded that one of the shells hit a roof. In any event, I have no reason to doubt anything in the reports that I've just read. I'm providing a photocopy of the relevant pages of my notes to accompany my statement." And then I asked General Nicolai: "Now, sir, I hope I have been accurate and complete in reading the entirety of this so we can have agreement. Would you stand by this paragraph of your 2006 written statement to the Office of the Prosecutor as being truthful and accurate and would you so testify today, subject to the solemn declaration that you have taken?" And his answer was: "Yes, I still do."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, does this briefing that he is talking about sound familiar to you? Are you aware of anything like that? That's a question for you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I never seen or heard anything about this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can call up in e-court 1D917. And I do have a hard copy, with the assistance of the usher, to provide to yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the full number of the 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes it is. 1D00917.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the first question I have for you, sir, is: Now looking at this document that you have in front of you, is this one of the documents that I gave you yesterday that you referenced earlier today?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 5 in the English in e-court and page 10 in the Serbian in e-court, and if we look at paragraph 23. Actually, it's the prior page in B/C/S; I apologise. And paragraph 23 we'll see is the one that I just read out from the transcript that we discussed with Colonel Nicolai. I'd like to look at the next paragraph with you and that's paragraph 24, and we'll need to go to the next page in the B/C/S to see that. And I will read the whole thing, which says: "I recall that it was very important that the source of fire be determined, because we did not rule out any possibility, including the possibility that the Bosniaks had shelled their own people. I have never seen or have any evidence that the Bosniaks shelled their own people, although I heard from my predecessor, General Van Baal, that it might have happened during his time. Elements to consider were that if there was no sound to be heard, the shell must have been fired from far away. And the fact that" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you're on your feet but I have heard nothing anything else but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a bit confusing for me if you're standing. I take it that you want to intervene in one way or another. If you just take a position on your seat [Overlapping speakers] ... if the time is there. At this moment, you said you would intervene later. What Mr. Ivetic is doing now is reading this portion of the statement to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I guess I could intervene right now. I think we've now gone a lot further and broached into an area where this has actually become a rather leading exercise and the fact of presenting information from another witness that the witness is not familiar about, hasn't seen before. There's no reason if counsel wants to cover topics or things like that, counsel can just ask him about it. This is a viva voce witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We do not know what the question is so, therefore, whether it will be leading or not is still unknown. But, the caveat is there, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Weber will jump up if you attach any leading question in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honours, and when I asked general questions, I get the objection from Mr. Weber that I should ask what documents and what the witness has before him so that's what I'm trying to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I guarantee you there will not be a leading question at the end of this. I'm just trying to provide the full context to the witness and then ask a non-leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Mr. Weber will be happy that you give him guarantees. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could scroll to the top of the English, I will, we should have the tail-end of this. I think we've missed a page. We should go back one page. We skipped two pages instead of one, it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the top we have the last part of the paragraph which I was just reading. Which says: "Cymbeline did not pick up anyone, meant that the trajectory was very low. I remember that the investigation brought us to the conclusion that it was the Serb forces who did the shelling. I don't remember the names of all the investigators, but I do remember that the chief UNMO was part of the team." Do you care to comment on this assertion of General Nicolai that the chief UNMO was part of the investigative team that concluded that the Serb forces did the shelling.

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Well, sir, in my head, the chief, only chief UNMO was the Brazilian general in Zagreb. Whether the Pakistani colonel in Sarajevo BiH command called himself chief UNMO, I don't recall, but that may have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, do you recall if either the Brazilian general in Zagreb or the Pakistani colonel in Sarajevo participated in the investigation by your UNMOs of the Markale market shelling?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you clarify your last answer. "Not at all," does that refer to your recollection or do you exclude the possibility that they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm positive that they never took part in any investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time I was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're right at the time for the first break. I speak fast but not enough to use the half a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to finish up on the topic that we had been discussing prior to the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At transcript page 10701 of our transcript, General Nicolai testified as follows in relation to P797, which is, again, the Baxter report which I don't know if you still have a hard copy of, but you don't need it for purposes of this question. But that's what he was asked about. And I will read for you the questions and the answers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will. "Mr. Ivetic: Thank you. If we can turn P797, which is the -- listed as the report, do you see on the first page this appears to be the final and comprehensive report of the Sarajevo mortar incident of 28 August 1995, I would like to turn to Annex B of this document, which is at page 9 of 21 in the English and page 9 of 24 in the B/C/S. "Q. And at the top we see that this is an UNMO daily sitrep, and it says released by Lieutenant-Colonel Oien, the SMO, does that refresh your recollection that this is the chief UNMO officer that verbally briefed you and other members of the BiH command as to the results of the preliminary results of the investigation that they performed? "A. The name doesn't really ring a bell or spur my recollection, but SMO stands for Senior Military Observer, as far as I know, so that must have been the rank or position. The name is not familiar to me."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I want to ask you, Colonel, is there any possibility that you would have met with or briefed General Nicolai of a result that is different than is written in the daily sitrep report that we looked at for the Markale shelling in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No, I -- I don't recall any kind of meeting with General Nicolai. And I -- no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could I kindly ask the usher to assist the witness in fixing the chair. Because the back of the chair is a little bit too flexible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We also have some chairs here. I don't know if it might be any better but it might be quicker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They sometimes don't co-operate when you manipulate the controls, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to either the Pakistani colonel who was in Sarajevo within the UNMO structure or the Brazilian general who was the chief UNMO in Zagreb, could either of them issue orders to your Sarajevo UNMOs to undertake investigations without going through you or without you knowing about it?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No. They had to go through our headquarter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, to return to the sitreps, if we could have in e-court 65 ter number 14296, and that is the hard copy that I had offered earlier, which now I have the correct number for it. So, with the assistance of the usher, it could first be shown again to opposing counsel and then to the witness. And now that we have both languages on the screen, sir, again I will ask you which UNMO HQ is the source of this sitrep?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: UNMO HQ Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know how these reports issued by the UNMO HQ Zagreb, how they compared with the reports that, for instance, your headquarter would issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- could Mr. Mladic speak at an inaudible volume. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Colonel, let me restart again. Do you know how these reports that would be issued by the UNMO HQ in Zagreb would compare with the reports that, for instance, your headquarters would issue?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Normally they should be compared, yes, and not letter by letter but it -- the results would compare, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this one is dated 29 August 1995. I would ask that we turn to page 21 in e-court and I think that's the page that I have marked for you with a Post-It note to make it easier since it is a lengthy document. And here we see, for instance, at the top: "One mortar tail-fin was recovered with batch markings [sic]," and several other bullet points that I think we all agree are pretty much the same as we saw in the -- in the sitreps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you said "markings," plural. I only see "marking."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise again. My eyes are not co-operating with me today when it comes to reading off the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said a tail-fin and there's no fin in that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So ... I should probably quit while I'm ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Give it another try.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We see here: "One more tail was recovered with batch marking number MK/M74/KB93070." And we can read all together the remainder of the text here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, how does this text compare to what your headquarters reported in relation to the Markale shelling incident on 28 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: This seems to be exactly the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can now look at P2608 again, and I again have a hard copy for you. And this is the one we already saw before the break so I won't ask you which headquarters would have issued it. But I will ask you this: The UNMO HQ Zagreb, just so that we're entirely clear, who was in charge of that HQ?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: In charge of that HQ, it was the Brazilian CMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And this daily sitrep is dated 30 August 1995. And if we turn to page 20 in e-court in English and page 36 and 37 in B/C/S, and, again, I have tabbed it with a Post-It note in the hard copy. I think we come to the part dealing with Sarajevo. And we see here under item number 2, Federation side, UNMO team Sedrenik was tasked to investigate the impacts in the general area of the marketplace (central city Sarajevo)," et cetera et cetera, and if we look at the very bottom of the page, we see the last bullet point that says, and it will be the next page in B/C/S. It says: "The bearing in combination with estimated angle of impact could not provide exact MOR position or an" - and if we go to the next page - "accurate origin of fire since it was not known with which charge the MOR projectiles were fired. Therefore range of firing position along bearing line could not be determined." And can you read the rest. But how does this compare to the UNMO sitrep that we looked at earlier released by Captain Ford at midnight on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: It's the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we're completed with that topic. Then I won't ask to go through any other ones with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That I believe 65 ter 14296 has not been offered into evidence yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, it has not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we then have it admitted at this time. It's been shown to the witness. He authenticated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's up to Your Honours. I read the part that we were looking at. I don't know if we need the whole -- it's a 27-page document according to my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We tender it. I mean, we've accepted the sitrep off similar length from the next day, P2608, the question that is arising, I believe, and I don't want to say too much in front of the witness, is what information was conveyed necessarily through to the UN HQ in Zagreb, and the Chamber should have a proper record of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, irrespective of whether the appropriate moment would have been cross-examination, if Mr. Weber is seeking to tender it where the Defence does not, does the Defence object?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then under those circumstances, perhaps a little bit earlier, but, Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7808, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7808 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, during your time-period as the SMO in the UNMO HQ in Sarajevo, was there ever any occasion where there was information available to the UNMO Sarajevo HQ seeming to indicate that the Bosnian Muslim government forces were shooting their own people in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I'm -- we suspected there was BiH firing into Sarajevo. We reported everything we saw. To -- to be -- to confirm that I have to read all my sitreps, of course, 20 years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you report anything you suspected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We reported facts. Only facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And there was -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So this suspicion you didn't report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. But I remember on one occasion than must have been in June or July, I was on leave, came back from a leave, and my OPS officer at the time, a Danish captain, he was gone when I was -- when I returned. And the case was this, that during my period of leave, I don't know what happened, he went down to the BiH liaison officers in sector -- in Sarajevo, and told them to stop firing at their own people. Which, of course, was a silly thing to do. And he was immediately declared persona non grata and sent home. If something happened, I could not -- I don't remember was confirmed, but I remember this thing, and that reminded me of that we -- we sometimes suspected, and, as I said earlier, I had to read my reports to confirm that we reported this as a fact, but then again we reported the facts, not what we suspected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question. You said which was a silly thing to do. Did you mean to say that it was silly to tell them or silly to shell your own people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, it was silly thing to go to confrontate this liaison officer. Because what we normally do, we objected by the normal channels or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know whether you can answer my next question which would be whether the declaration of persona non grata, whether such would have been reported as a fact although it happened in your absence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I used the phrase persona non grata. He was not wanted there anymore and had to leave immediately. Because if he didn't leave, they would stop the co-operation with us and we didn't want that. So that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that that must have been reported [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... so, yes, that was reported. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I take it that the underlying facts may be traceable for the parties in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I forget, sir, if I asked you, do you remember the name of the Danish officer or his rank?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: It was captain, was it Hansen? Hansen? It's a common Danish name so I believe it was Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. On behalf of my client and the Defence team. I thank you for answering our questions. Those are all the questions that I have for you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Oien, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You find Mr. Weber to your right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, just so you are aware, I will probably be significantly shorter than my original estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All parties are surprising the Chamber by being considerably shorter than they announced. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel Oien. Oien?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Oien.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Sir, today, I just have some very straightforward questions for you. If you could please listen to my questions and I'll try to move along rather efficiently. Could you tell us the exact date that you arrived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was before Easter that year. It must have been in the beginning of March. I don't -- I don't remember -- I'm sorry, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. It was around March 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning of March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You just mentioned that you referred to a Danish UNMO, a captain, Captain Hansen. This was Captain Thomas Hansen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That may be correct, yes. I'm not good at names but Thomas Hansen rings a bell for me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay, and this incident that he was referring about was the shelling of the RTV building in Sarajevo on 28th June 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I couldn't say yes because I don't remember the actual incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you something quickly to see if it refreshes your recollection. Could the Prosecution please have 1D00796. Sir, this is a statement that was provided by Captain Hansen to the investigators of the OTP. I take it you've never seen this statement before?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the statement. Sir, I'm going to direct your attention to the middle of the page. This is where Captain Hansen states that he investigated the shelling of the TV building on 28 June 1995 that caused approximately 30 civilian casualties. In the third paragraph from the bottom, he states: "I was informed by an UNMO who had seen the shelling on the TV building that this particular bomb that impacted in the TV building was fired from the BiH side. Another UNMO who heard the bomb told me that the bomb only flew for a short period, so that the [sic] fitted with the findings of the first UNMO that the bomb was fired from BiH ... territory." Does this refresh your recollection and sound like the event that related to Captain Hansen?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, this was in June, as I said. I believe this episode happened in June, but personally I was not there. And if this was the facts, of course, you can find it in the report from the 28th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have D147.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this Trial Chamber has actually received a good deal of evidence related to the shelling of the TV building on 28th of June. This is one document that's in evidence that's related to it. It is a Sarajevo-Romanija Corps report dated 30 June 1995 from Commander Dragomir Milosevic. In the bottom half of the page before you, General Milosevic states: "Our artillery forces are responding with precision to the Muslim artillery attacks. In one such response on 28 June, they hit the BH RTC, radio and television centre, the centre of media lies against the just struggle of the Serbian people." The fact is UNMO Hansen's belief was wrong and, in fact, it's the Serbs who, as seen in their own document, that shelled the TV building on 28 June; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: You ask me? I can't tell you. I don't remember. I was not there and I can't confirm anything of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Mr. Weber. You say, and that's how it is recorded: "The fact is UNMO Hansen's belief was wrong and, in fact, it was the Serbs who had seen their own document that shelled the TV building."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I phrased it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Two things --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honour, for clarifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since, since you've commented on what you believe you've heard from Captain Hansen what I'm putting to you is that what Captain Hansen believed to have heard was wrong, that it was incorrect information, and as we see here in a document from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, it was the Serb artillery who, in fact, shelled the TV building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I think the witness has already --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the question and the phrasing of the question, unless you misunderstood the question but I take it from the answer you did not but at least it's now, I think it's clarified that what Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It did, except Mr. Weber that when reading -- look, this document on the screen, I'm not sure who the "they" refer to. "In one such response on the 28th June, they hit ..." Who are the "they"? The "they," SRK forces or the "they," Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's why I read the immediately preceding sentence to that because I think that makes it clear. Dragomir Milosevic states: "Our artillery forces are responding with precision to the Muslim artillery attacks. In such a -- in one such response, on 28 June, they hit the BH RTC building."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am with you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, only for the record, I think that the description of what's in Mr. Hansen's statement in relation to this document is not entirely accurate since it was the UNMO observer who saw the bomb launched, not Mr. Hansen who said that it came from the BiH side. And Mr. Weber has left out that in that time period there were a lot of homemade air bombs that landed in that area, which is the next part of Mr. Hansen's statement so we don't know exactly -- you know, which -- we -- we don't know -- it's -- to say that the truth is when there's a multiple projectiles in an area without having presented -- you know, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are -- if there's any evidence about other impacts on the RTV building then, of course, the Chamber would like to have a closer look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The statement we just looked at says at that time -- pardon me. "In that period there were a lot of homemade airline bombs that landed in that area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it's about hitting the RTV. Landing in the area is not the same as hitting the RTV building. So, therefore, if there's any evidence which would multiply the hits on the RTV building, of course, the Chamber would be interested to -- unless it is there already, but you'll forgive me for, and you'll forgive the Chamber for not knowing all the details that we have to look at it. But if there's any reason to accept that on 28 June several -- several projectiles hit the RTV building then, of course, we'd like to -- we'd like if you would draw our attention to that evidence or present such evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the Markale shelling on 28th of August. Do you recall where you were at on the morning of 28 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I often used that road. As a rule I didn't stay much in my headquarter. I was out visiting my teams to get a better idea of the situation, and I often used that road and I think I passed the Markale area about 20 minutes before the shelling and went to my headquarter. Then in my headquarter, we got this phone call reporting the shelling and after the team was tasked and started their investigation I went back to the area, just as I said earlier, to ensure that they had good working conditions and if they needed any kind of support from the HQ. Then I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Oien, you were asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. This document is provisionally under seal, Mr. Weber. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The SRK report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what Mr. Registrar tells me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not appreciate that. I don't believe it's not necessarily due to the document itself but due to maybe the -- the -- the individual who it came through. I actually don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the document is under seal or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes -- N -- for the reasons is another matter -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, it should not be broadcasted and I do understand that there's no major concern about it having been broadcasted --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- until now. That being clarified, I think it was -- yes, I -- I intervened because protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto would have one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Oien, in response to a question where were you on the morning of the 28th July 1995, you answered I used that road. Now, just for the record, which road was this that you used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it was a street in Sarajevo where the Markale incident happened. I used that street when driving to my teams and wherever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to answer the question that was put to you? Where were you on the morning of the 28th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The morning I started in the headquarter and then I went out, passed that area, came back to the headquarter and later on at about 11:00 or something, we got the task to investigate this incident. And, as I said, after about 20 minutes or so when my team was at the spot, I went back, just to ensure that they had good working conditions and if they needed any support from the HQ. And then I went back to the headquarter which was in the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P797 and if we could please go straight away to page 9 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we see that this is the sitrep that you released on the 28th of August. You've looked at this already today. I just want to draw your attention to the fact that there's a -- underneath your name a to line and then a list of a number of UN HQs, two of them, and then an info and a list of another -- some more UNMO HQs. Is it correct that the information contained in the sitreps would be regularly reported upwards to the UNMO HQ in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this sitrep covers just until 1800 hours in the day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please go to page 13 of both versions, and if we could please go one more page forward actually in page -- in the B/C/S. Sir, on this page of the sitrep you released, subsection looks like d. 1(C) states: "UNMO investigation so far has determined:" And then if we could have the next page in the English, and then I direct your attention also back down to the fact that the -- that says in the parentheses, "The full incident report will follow this daily sitrep when team has reported -- has concluded investigation and reported to this HQ." Sir, at the time of this sitrep the investigation was still ongoing; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe, so. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 15 of the original document and page 16 of the B/C/S translation. Now, this is the update that was commented upon by you earlier today. We see that it was prepared by Captain Ihab and released by Captain Ford, as you've already stated. Was this done because you were no longer present at the UNMO HQ, that is, released by Captain Ford?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: As I remember the normal procedure it was that the OPS officer related the daily sitrep and he was always there at the end of the day. So that was the normal procedure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that the first time that you saw this update in the fall of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't remember when -- if I was in the HQ when this report was -- was done, so I don't remember if it was the same night or the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution now go to Exhibit P2608. This was the UNMO HQ Zagreb daily sitrep, and we see that there's a line that is just above the top -- the -- the middle of the page that says "info by CAPSAT," and one of the UNMO HQs that are listed is Sector Sarajevo. I think you've basically indicated this so far, but this was a part of the UNMO HQ in Sarajevo reporting information to the HQ in Zagreb; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, the information we -- we reported was then in the HQ Zagreb sitrep and what was packed, as you can see as one of the addresses on this one. So we had the HQ Zagreb sitrep every day so we could follow what was happening what was in all areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And we see that this daily sitrep covers the period immediately following the update that we just looked at. It indicates 29 Aug 1995, 0001 hours, to 2359 hours; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 24 of the original and page 41 of the B/C/S. On this page, we see a summary of meetings. The information includes about -- at approximately 1100 hours on 29th, team leader Sedrenik participated in the second meeting of the special joint investigation team. Team leader -- team leader of team Sedrenik that would have been Lieutenant-Colonel Konings; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And Colonel Konings was involved in meetings and providing information to people concerning the course of his investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Say again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the course of Colonel Konings's investigation into the shelling of the 28th of August, he was involved in meetings that would provide information about the course of his investigation?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, there was -- it was a joint investigation team with the Bosnian police and I believe, I'm not sure, but then also the French engineers but they co-operated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the first bullet point that immediately follows the sentence: "The following details should be added to the report of this incident forwarded with the daily sitrep and sitrep update for 28 August and the interim daily sitrep for 29 August." That bullet point states: "During the time-frame of the five impacts, team Sedrenik members operating from OP-1 neither saw nor heard any outgoing mortar rounds from either the BiH army territory or from BSA army territory." This was information that was added after the sitrep and sitrep update; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes. That seems correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this was known by 29 August 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That may be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just go to a few other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, UNMOs -- I'm going to change topics. I'm going to ask you something general here. UNMOs provided reports on the investigations that they carried out during the course of their patrols; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 28529. This is an UNMO HQ Sarajevo patrol report from 15 March 1995 related to a report of a killed BSA soldier. You received patrol reports like this one; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English version and page 3 of the B/C/S, and directing your attention towards the bottom half of the page. On this page, we see that the UNMOs met with Captain Mile, the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Romanija Brigade, we see that Captain Mile expressed his anger about BiH activity and the Egyptian Battalion. At point d, the report indicates Captain Mile was overheard telling his commander to go back to his position and inform his troops to fire on anything that moved. Soldiers, civilians, et cetera. On the same point, if we could also look at another document and if the Prosecution could have 65 ter 15120, this is a patrol report from the same UNMOs the next day, the 16th of March, 1995, under point 7, the report relates information obtained from soldiers on the confrontation line where the fatality occurred. Among other things they claimed that before they would only shoot at armed soldiers but now this has changed and they will open fire on anyone, on anybody who moves, including women and children. Later on, it indicates that these threats echo very much the statements made the day before by the battalion commander. Were you aware that members of the BSA felt it was acceptable to retaliate against civilians in Sarajevo for deaths of their own soldiers? Are these the types of reports you received?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the mischaracterisation of Sarajevo. This is in relation to the CFL, which I believe is the confrontation line, which is a limited area of Sarajevo, not Sarajevo as a whole, as Mr. Weber has presented. All this has been in relation to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I put my question fairly. It's an investigation in relation to a shooting that occurred along the confrontation line. I believe the witness is capable of answering the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness should be very well aware, because that's a concern of Mr. Ivetic, that what triggered this event was an event which happened close to the confrontation line, if I understand well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The document is talking about what said what would happen at the CFL, at the confrontation line, that they had only been shooting at soldiers but after this incident they would shoot at anything that moved in the confrontation line. That's the plain language he did not mention to this witness [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let's go through it in detail. Let's go back to the previous document, what the sentence that was overheard to start with, because that's the factual starting point for it. Let's go back to that. And, witness, may I specifically ask your attention for the details of the language which was read to you as to what was overheard and what was later reported. Could we go back to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was 65 ter 28529, page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would you slowly read what exactly was overheard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll read point d verbatim. Under point 2, it states: "He told his commander of that area to go back to his position and inform his troops to fire on anything that moved soldiers, civilians, et cetera (this last point was not told to SE 12, just overheard as we were leaving his location)..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was then the language which was overheard. And now we move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution go back to then 65 ter 15120. And, Your Honours, I'll read the entirety of item 7.
