utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under patrol commander's comments, it states: "Soldiers on the confrontation line," denoted as CFL, "at location of fatality said that the cease-fire agreement no longer existed in their AOR. Before they would only shoot at armed soldiers but now this has changed and they will open fire on any body who moves including women and children. Also said was that they know" - in the text it appears as the word "were" - "the UNPROFOR OP is, in that area, and that they would fire at this if this is what it takes to stop [sic] sniping activity in this area. These threats echo very much the statements made yesterday by BN commander and were reported to SX/R1. Tension continues to rise in this area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, put your question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just for clarity BN refers to battalion commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: BN, that would be the battalion commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this was information that was reported up to you, information like this; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, that must be correct. If it is from my UNMOs, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were aware that BSA soldiers were willing to not only shoot at soldiers but also at women and children; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the question, it misstates the document again. The document has been talking about in the area, in the confrontation line. That missing from the question [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Ivetic, as far as shooting at civilians it's not limited. The position of those shooting may be those one close to the confrontation line, but as far as the targeting of civilians, it would be anyone, irrespective of their distance. At least the document doesn't give any information about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The prior one does. The prior document does, it says in that same area. That's why I'm objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In that same area but it doesn't say where the civilians to be targeted are found. Of course, you can't shoot to an area in which you are not. But it's -- it happened at the confrontation line. That's at least what the document says. Let's leave -- Mr. Weber, you could also from refrain from rephrasing it. You could say that this overheard passage of shooting at civilians, and the comments given later, I take it that you have a question about whether that was common or appropriate or whatever your question is -- will be, but let's not rephrase. The witness has read the relevant portions. It was read to him, as a matter of fact, could you please phrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to re-ask my last question which I think was okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were aware that BSA soldiers were willing to not only shoot at soldiers but also at women and children; correct?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I was not aware of that at that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the document two documents into evidence, 65 ter 15120 and 65 ter 28529.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object if the Prosecution is reopening their case to present evidence that this witness did not testify about in direct and did not have the any additional facts to talk about, I'd like to hear the arguments for why Prosecution is reopening their case. But I believe their case should be closed and so they can't lead additional evidence that they did not lead during their case. The 65 ter number of this document shows it was their possession throughout this case and so their choice to now try to lead positive evidence without seeking rebuttal or reopening, I believe is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is fair. The witness has been called to testify about his time in Sarajevo. The counsel broadened that examination beyond to what even we thought would be noticed, with mainly dealt with the Markale incident to discuss the potential of who was motivated to fire at whom in Sarajevo, intonating that there was a potential firing incident involving Captain Hansen targeting -- that he had information the ABiH targeting themselves. I think it's fair game at that point to confront the witness and find out actually what he knew or aware of based on documents that would have been available to him at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- which is why it's being put to the witness, because he was in a position where patrol reports, as he has already indicated, like this would have come to him about these investigations, so I believe he is the proper witness to confront with this information based on the testimony he has provided to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber postpones its decision on the admission and, Mr. Registrar, the number under which it will be marked for identification would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 28529 will be MFI P7809. And 65 ter 15120 will be marked for identification P7810.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the postponement deals with both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They are marked for identification, I think I said already that number should be assigned for that purpose and they hereby are marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You did say that, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now one item which it was about D147 which was provisionally under seal, Mr. Ivetic, could I just ask you, invite you, to read paragraph -- transcript page 7808, where, in relation to, among others, this document, I asked; have you carefully considered whether some of them have to be under seal?" Mr. Lukic, you then answered, "I haven't. I haven't checked. We have to check which ones should be admitted under seal." And that's what triggered it to be provisionally under seal. Now, this happened a little bit over three years ago. Mr. Lukic, I think we've given you a fair period of time to consider whether D147 should be under seal, yes or no. We'd like to receive a response within the next week. Any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have D00139. And hopefully I've got the number right this time. And if I do, I have a hard copy for the witness, which might be easier. If we can have the English on one of the sides of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for that, sir, you have been asked about UNMO patrol reports. Are you familiar with the format of this document that is before you on the screen and that you have a hard copy of? Is this an official format of an UNMO patrol report?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for this one, in particular, we see the date -- am I reading the date correctly as being 29 August 1995? Is that the correct --

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: That seems correct to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we see here it says PTL leader LTC Konings. Do you believe that to be the same person you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PTL members.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, but the first one says, "PTL leader" and then "member." We're both correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're both correct, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here I direct everyone's attention to the handwritten part and the second paragraph of the handwritten part, which I will try to read slowly: "This report is related to the UNMO packet report" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about patrol report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It could be patrol, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just give a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree. "... issued on the 28th of August, 1995, copy of this report has been made available for the investigation team." And then if we go to the next page of the document, here we have the notes of meetings with various pens from the joint investigative team. And if we look at the PTL/LDR's remarks, first of all, PTL/LDR's remarks, whose remarks would those be? It's above the item number 1 at the bottom. It looks like a 5 heading number 5, and it says, PTL/LDR's remarks. Who is that referring to?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: To me it looks like the team leader, the platoon leader, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, in the B/C/S translation, it's about a patrol rather than a platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a patrol, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So patrol leader's remarks. That's how you understand it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we see there that there's 1, 2 and 3. It talks about some facts are slightly different from the lists that UNMO received as to casualties, et cetera, and then item number 3 appears to say: "All the facts inserted in the first report remain unchanged and valid." And then there's a signature, again it looks like LTC Konings. Does this comport with your recollection of the results after the patrol had their meetings with the BiH joint investigative team as to the Markale shelling in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PER OIVIND OIEN
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen this report before, but the conclusion is that it's correct. The facts remain unchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Colonel, again, I thank you for answering all of our questions and that completes our examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Oien, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no more witnesses to -- at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, as I threatened already in the begin of today's session, we had close to 20 procedural items, and the Chamber suggests that we spend the remainder of the day to deal with those. We all know it is not the most exciting and the most challenging part to hear about new translations, et cetera, so, therefore, the Chamber fully understands that if Mr. Mladic would rather do other things than to follow these administrative proceedings, but at the same time, of course, it's part of the case and he is fully entitled to be present. I leave it in his hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, of course, we would take a break first anyhow, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it is probably agreeable to take the break and we'll determine during the break what [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Then perhaps also during the break, we might consider whether there are a few more questions about matters about scheduling, especially, so not administrative matters. And if Mr. Mladic would wish to leave after we've dealt with scheduling issues and be relieved from the administrative matters, that, of course, is entirely in his own hands. We would just like to be informed. We take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber was informed that Mr. Mladic had decided that he did not wish to further be present and that he even would prefer not to come to court to tell this but that he would convey this message through you. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's absolutely accurate, Your Honour, everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber establishes that Mr. Mladic waives his right to be present during the remainder of today's hearing. And I'd now like to -- if you just allow me to check one thing very quickly. Yes. I'd like -- I would first like to start with issues related to scheduling. We first move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. As the Defence has confirmed that it has dropped Witness GRM-274, the Chamber refrains from making any follow-up decisions in relation to this witness. The Chamber also declares the motion for protective measures for this witness moot. Then -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next item starts on the 15th of December, 2015, when the witness statement of Jasmin Odobasic was conditionally admitted into evidence, pending the filing of an attestation and declaration in compliance with Rule 92 bis. On the 16th of February of this year, the Defence informed the Chamber via e-mail that the witness had refused to sign his statement. The Defence also requested the Chamber's guidance on issuing a subpoena to compel him to sign the attestation. The Chamber responded on the 25th of February, via e-mail, that such a subpoena would defeat its purpose but that the Defence can file a motion for the issuance of a subpoena to compel the witness to testify and to consider the potential for his testimony to be heard through videolink. And that's all hereby put on the record. Next item deals with a Defence request for leave to reply. On the 23rd of February of this year, the Defence requested leave to reply in relation to its third bar table motion and also requested a seven-day extension to file its reply. On the 26th of February, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that it does not oppose the extension. And on the 29th of February, the Chamber granted both requests, and that decision is hereby placed on the record. I now would like to go briefly through the outstanding issues, as far as witnesses are concerned, and I would like to state as a starting point the e-mail which was sent by Mr. Ivetic on the 19th of February. The first item was about the witness whose testimony we have heard today and, therefore, doesn't need our further attention. Although it talks about two Norwegian witnesses but that's dealt with as well. And that's what the Defence -- what Mr. Ivetic explains in further detail in the second -- in the following paragraph in his e-mail. I now move to a witness, Mr. ... one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness is, if I can call him the Belgian witness, Mr. Ivetic, then I think we all understand who I am referring to, there seem to be no further objections for him to testify and we especially are envisaging the -- to receive the testimony under Rule 92 ter on the basis of a statement already taken. On the 19th of February, you indicated that the 92 ter motion was filed for the same on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. It was either that day or the next day but it is filed as we sit here today. We are still awaiting for the one approval from the other entity though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Do we have any idea, and perhaps I put this in kind of a general question, when the Defence intends to call these witnesses because it may not be very efficient to have half a day here, another half a day there, and to see whether we can concentrate it on a certain period of time. That's -- I now move to the next one, which is a witness who has contacted the Defence on the 16th of February, as we read in your e-mail, a witness who has received documents and questions but we see that there are also administrative matters which cause some problems. Now, the Chamber very much appreciates if it is informed about problems, but the Chamber would be -- at least as much interested in receiving information about how to resolve them. I have referred to this witness as one of the pending items for scheduling and that it is unlikely that he would appear in the first two weeks of March seems to be obvious as well. I then move to the next one in which the Defence informs the Chamber that Rule 70 approval is still not obtained. And then the Defence informs the Chamber that they will file a 92 ter motion for him on that same day or the following Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe that was filed on the following Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll not further elaborate on that at this very moment. Then, the next witness mentioned in your e-mail, Mr. Ivetic, is a witness you had not been able to get contact with, and you tried to contact him through e-mail, and you were unsuccessful. Any follow-up on that witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We still have not been able to effectuate or locate a good mailing address for him in the country where he is said to be situated, based upon the Rule 70 provider which told us that he emigrated from their country to this country so we have nothing in a positive report about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have further steps been initiated, apart from trying to find an e-mail address through official authorities or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have and the official authorities in the country where he is said to be located have declined to assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you have accepted that or are you seeking the assistance of the Chamber? And when was it that they declined?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The last communication I had with them, I think was perhaps a month, month and a half ago. And that's when I started pursuing other means such as private services for locating people [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... sometimes the Chamber can assist in -- and since six weeks passed since your unsuccessful efforts, there's not one road that leads to Rome sometimes there are more roads that lead -- well, physical persons can not travel on more roads but legal procedures can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand. And we'll take your suggestion under advisement and we'll act accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not a suggestion. I regret that I have to establish that at least, that option has not been further explored for the last six weeks. Then, I move on to the next, which is the two expert witnesses. The witnesses Stankovic and Radovanovic and we have received the report, the 21st report, and it is stated that they are not available now. Again, and that's the overall question, at the end of going through your e-mail is what does the -- I don't know if I have to address you, Mr. Ivetic, or lead counsel, Mr. Lukic, what are the plans of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have filed one 94 bis for Dr. Stankovic. We have just gotten the report translated and are preparing to file what would be a supplemental 94 bis for the additional material that goes beyond the Dunjic report. Under my understanding then of the guidance that Your Honours gave at the beginning of the case, the expert witnesses can't be scheduled until the Rule 94 bis process has been completed which would be at least a month for that. The last translation that was outstanding from CLSS as to Professor Radovanovic has been received and now has been sent to her and we're hoping to hear from her in the next day or so, as to when she can expect to complete her report as to Tomasica. In which case, the 94 bis will be prepared as soon as the translation is available and again, therefore, they would not be available to testify until at least, I would imagine, probably month and a half. I don't know -- I don't know at this stage how large the report is since it's not completed, but I don't anticipate it being too lengthy so as to take too long to translate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said, and I was a bit confused about -- you have received the translation? Outstanding translation, but there are other translations still to be [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We've received both of the ones mentioned in the report. One was just received, I think, Friday, if I remember it correctly, and the other one was received earlier than that. And so now we have both of those that were mentioned as outstanding with relation to Professor Radovanovic sent to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but is there any need for further translations. You said "complete the report," what is there to be still completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The report has to be drafted and is drafted in B/C/S, and therefore, needs to be translated into English, so that we can use it in these proceedings. That's how all the prior expert reports of Ms. Radovanovic were done, in B/C/S, and therefore there's a translation from B/C/S to English, the official language of the Tribunal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when did you expect that you could present such a report to CLSS?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As I indicated, considering that the translation of the last document was sent just yesterday, I hoped to talk with Professor Radovanovic either today or tomorrow to ascertain how much additional time is needed for her to complete her report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's just to include now the latest two documents. Were they lengthy ones or were they ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The one was a lengthy one. It was a 100 UN pages for translation, which is why the translation service needed more time to do the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the other one was?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would hazard 20 pages. I don't know the exact number, but I think 20 pages is probably at the maximum, at the higher end of the approximation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in itself, the length of a document does not necessarily tell us a lot about the impact on the final drafting. I mean, a lengthy document could be just one footnote. Therefore, we're wondering when we'll hear from you that the reports are finalized.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we have been reporting every week, by the end of the week. And so, by the end of this week, you will definitely know the latest information I have. And if I have a date certain, you'll have a date certain. I basically report what I hear back from the field, from the legal assistant who is meeting directly with the experts and then I also have direct communications with the experts themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber would appreciate if, in the next report, you would tell us more about these two documents that were delivered only recently by CLSS so that we can take that into account when considering how much extra time should perhaps be granted or where we would push you even further to present the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can do that right now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They're both articles by Ewa Tabeau that were not disclosed to us by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An article of Ewa Tabeau of 100 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, 100 UN pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know that UN pages are not the same as pages for normal people. Both were -- okay. And do you, by any way, have the titles of these? Are these focussing specifically on this case or are they general?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Focussing on sources used and focussing on the -- Bosnia but not dealing with this case or the testimony that was in this case. But dealing with methodology, demographic sources, procedures, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say they were not disclosed. I take that it that this information is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they knew about them. They're not dealing with the Tribunal. They're published in outside journals that we uncovered and that therefore we had to have translations. Usually, if the Prosecution discloses it, we would have translations into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that point. So there was no claim that there was a duty to disclose.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there any reason now why it is only now that these -- I mean, I take it that these articles were not published last month.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They weren't published last month, but they were not discovered -- I don't remember if they were published after the witness testified. I don't have that recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to know from when these articles -- when these articles were published in order to establish to what extent it is reasonable to ask additional time for them to be translated and to be made part of the report. That's about the last two, Mr. Ivetic, and, as I said before, I don't know whether to address you. Perhaps I should do in relation to the experts, but all the other witnesses, what are the plans in relation to them? Do you want to have a concentrated week, or two weeks where you want to present them? Well, let's say in six weeks from now, eight weeks from now, or four weeks from now? What are the plans?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The plans would be to have them concentrated in one sitting or session, whatever that would be and the determining factor, I think is probably centred around the experts since their times are fixed. I suspect, since the other entity that I've been working with has been always rather quick in getting back to me and promised they would have indicated any problems, that I should shortly be getting approval for the Belgian. So then it would just be a matter of picking a date that works for him which shouldn't be an issue, since the proximity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, we have some witnesses, for example, I expressed my regrets that six weeks had passed without seeking the assistance of the Chamber, that means that there is still quite a lot of uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to that one, that's correct. With respect to the other one that is below the Belgian, I'm about 90 per cent certain that we'll not be calling that witness. You'd not asked for us to comment, but I do want to make sure that you know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, it's entirely up to you to give up certain efforts to try and get those witnesses in The Hague, yes or no. The Chamber just waits and offers as always its assistance, if needed. Then let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, of course, it would be nice if everyone would be in one or two weeks together, but the Chamber does certainly not insist if that would delay the overall hearing of that evidence to keep the expert witnesses together with the other witnesses we're still waiting for. Whatever is done is done. And also because what we now hear that the reason for the delay in the work of the experts is the access to articles which may be - the Chamber doesn't know yet - may have been published long ago, therefore the Chamber will have to assess also to what extent that justifies further delays. Therefore, we'd like to hear from you a clear plan. That week, week 20, week 18, week 16, that's when we plan to hear this evidence. The Chamber is relying on you to organise it properly and would like to receive your plans, well, let's say, within a week from now, that we have then -- we know more about the experts. You may have made progress in your contact with the other witnesses, or at least one of them, and with one of the authorities which has to give the green light, so the Chamber would like to get that information -- well, it's not a strict deadline. I mean, a week -- well, let's say not later than next week, Wednesday [Realtime transcript read in error "witness"].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I add to this that the time which is elapsing now, the Chamber considers this time as time already available for preparing for the next stages of the proceedings even if there's one or two articles still to be -- to be adopted in an expert report, that should not refrain -- that shouldn't keep the Defence off from preparing the next stages of the witnesses. So that is -- I think we expressed that before, that is emphasised again, that waiting for this evidence to be received does not relieve you from your duty to already prepare for the next stages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To avoid any misunderstanding for the record, page 64, last word in line 25 it should read Wednesday, not witness. That means -- let's say not later than next week, Wednesday, as the Presiding Judge said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can imagine that having heard the witnesses -- the word witness so many times that this is what happens. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I ask for clarification. You are recorded as saying at line 6 of page 65, "that shouldn't keep the Defence off from preparing the next stage of the witnesses." Does that refer to the rebuttal case of the Prosecution? Because we have not had any filings yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever follows. We are at a stage where you could already work, for example, on final briefs even if you have not the full 100 per cent of evidence available. Perhaps not knowing what rebuttal evidence will still be heard. But you're supposed to start with preparing the next stages and then, of course, if there is any rebuttal evidence then it may well be that you have to change or to adapt to that new situation. But we would not like to hear in a couple of months from now, it's only know that we could start preparing final briefs, final argument, et cetera, even if you cannot complete that for the full 100 per cent, there's quite some substance that can be dealt with already in those early stages and the mere fact that there are still three, four, five witnesses from which we would receive evidence, doesn't mean that you could not yet work on those stages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So in the places of witnesses [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So in the place of witnesses in that sentence you can read case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any questions or observations in relation to the scheduling issues we dealt with? If not, then we'll now deal with the exciting administrative matters, as you are used to hear from us. I start with the remaining issues from the testimony of Dusan Pavlovic. During the testimony of Dusan Pavlovic, a number of exhibits were marked for identification pending English translations. The Defence has since informed the Prosecution and the Chamber, via e-mail, that the relevant translations have been uploaded into e-court. The Prosecution does not object to the translations. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the following: Doc ID 1D28-1967 to D1375; doc ID 1D28-1939 to D1378; doc ID 1D28-1796 to D1384, and to avoid any doubt, D1384 shall remain under seal; doc ID 1D28-1799 to D1385; doc ID 1D28-1802 to D1386; doc ID 1D28-1951 to D1395; and doc ID 1D28-1828 to D1398. All of the exhibits I just mentioned are admitted into evidence. And, as I said, D1384, still under seal. We stay with Mr. Dusan Pavlovic for the following. On the 2nd of February of this year, P7792 and D1401 were marked for identification pending the provision of English translations. On the 9th of February, the Prosecution informed the Defence and the Chamber, via an e-mail, that the English translations had been uploaded into e-court, and the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach doc ID Y039-9334-ET to P7792; and replace the place holder currently attached to D1401 with doc ID X019-9209-1. P7792 and D1401 are hereby admitted into evidence. P7792 shall remain under seal, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. On the -- the next item deals with P7638. On the 3rd of February of this year, the Chamber instructed the rear to assign exhibit number P7638 to document bearing Rule 65 ter number 06754a. P7638 is hereby admitted into evidence, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I now deal with some miscellaneous exhibits admitted into evidence and placed provisionally under seal. On the 3rd of February of this year, the Chamber, first that put on the record that it will invite the parties to communicate with the Republic of Serbia to see whether it intends to file a Rule 54 bis motion in relation to exhibits P7651, P7652, P7751, P7786, P7724, P7462, P5090, and D1288, all admitted under seal; and, second, instructed the Registry to lift the confidentiality of these exhibits within six weeks, unless the Republic of Serbia files a motion to keep them confidential by that date. On the 4th of February, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that protective measures are not required for six of the eight exhibits, being: P7651, P7652, P7724, P7462, P5090, and D1288. The Chamber therefore instructs the Registry to lift the confidentiality of those six exhibits. In order to avoid any doubt, the Chamber reiterates its instruction to the Registry to lift the confidentiality of the remaining two exhibits, P7751 and P7786, if the Republic of Serbia does not file a Rule 54 bis motion in relation to these documents by March 16, 2016. I move onto my next item, issues relating to the testimony of Mitar Kovac. On 19th of November of last year, P7674 was marked for identification pending the provision of English translation. On 8th of February of this year, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that the translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0562-0067-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translation to P7674 and admits it into evidence. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. Also on the 19th of February of last year, P7675 was reserved for an excerpt of the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 05580. On the 8th of February of this year, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that the proposed excerpt had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 05580a. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign P7675 to this excerpt and admits into evidence, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I now to move to issues relating to the testimony of GRM-116. On 16th of December, 2015, P7783, P7784, and P7785 were marked for identification pending the provision of B/C/S translations. On the 4th of February of this year, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that the translations had been uploaded into e-court under doc IDs 0687-0338-BCSDT, 0687-0341-BCSDT, and 0687-0409-BCSDT respectively. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translations to P7783, P7784, and P7785 respectively and admits them into evidence, under seal, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. Also on the 16th of December of last year, P7788 was marked for identification, pending agreement between the parties as to which sections of the document should be tendered. On the 4th of February, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that it tenders the document as currently uploaded in e-court. The Chamber hereby admits P7788 into evidence under seal, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I now to move to some remaining issues from the testimony of Zorica Subotic, and I start with P7574, which is a VRS Main Staff letter which was admitted into evidence on the 8th of October 2015. On the 23rd of December, the Chamber invited the Prosecution via e-mail to upload an English translation into e-court. The Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence on the 11th of January of this year, advising that an English translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0627-7518-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the English translation to Exhibit P7574 and gives the Defence one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I move to P7566 in relation to which there may be some confusion as whether this exhibit, a video, was admitted into evidence, as the words "admitted into evidence" do not appear in the transcript, and I refer you to page 39847. The Chamber hereby puts it on the record that Exhibit P7566 was admitted into evidence on the 7th of October, 2015. I move to D1270. On the 30th of September, 2015, Rule 65 ter number 33106, a MUP report, was marked for identification as D1270 pending a response from the Defence. On the 7th of October, the Prosecution tendered D1270. On the 8th of December, the Defence informed the Chamber via an e-mail that it intended to tender Rule 65 ter 1D05545 rather than 65 ter 33106. On the 9th of December, the Chamber e-mailed the parties instructing the Defence to put its position in relation to Rule 65 ter number 33106 on the record. That same day, the Defence objected to the admission of the document. Accordingly, the Chamber instructs the Registry to ensure that Rule 65 ter number 1D05545 is assigned to D1270. The question I raise is whether there are any objections against admission by the Prosecution? D1270, in the absence of any response to my last question, remains MFI'd until an English translation has been provided. Further, does the Prosecution still want to tender Rule 65 ter number 33106?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll have to get back to you on it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can do so within a week and since there may be no hearings, you can do that in the informal way as often practiced. I move to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, if I may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I note that we informed the Chamber that we discussed on these documents for a long time, and I know that now, under number 35 in our new chart, joint submission by the Prosecution and the Defence, you can find 33106a, which would be a new document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's actually B and H MUP reports relating to a shelling of Safeta Zajke street, number 43, on 24th of May 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it wasn't uploaded and I know that we agreed that the Prosecution has to upload that document. And I don't know if that has been done yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it, Mr. Traldi, that you would express your appreciation for the assistance given to you by Mr. Lukic and you will include this information in your brief report which the Chamber expects to receive within one week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We will. And it is in e-court now. The document that Mr. Lukic referred to, 65 ter 33106a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was whether you wanted to tender that. I take it that if you uploaded it and you discussed it with Mr. Lukic, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's part of our joint submission that we want to tender it, both parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A very practical question now for me is whether we will deal with it separately now at this moment or as part of the joint submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would rather deal with it as part of joint submission, not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll keep that until we deal with the submission as a whole. Thank you for your clarification. I now move to the next item on my agenda, is the remaining issue from the testimony of Mile Poparic and it's about D1340 for which on 5th of November, 2015, a number was reserved. It's a video on shelling and sniping incidents. On 9 November, the Chamber received an e-mail from the Defence advising that the surrogate sheet for the video was uploaded into e-court under document bearing Rule 65 ter number 1D05911A. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign D1340 to the surrogate sheet and admits D1340 into evidence, and the Prosecution has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. And I take it that the video was handed over in hard copy on the CD. I hear no cries, so, therefore, I take it that the assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that in the absence of Mr. Mladic, we'll not stop now after one hour but that we'll continue, and then most likely, if we deal with it within the next half an hour to adjourn for the day. The next item are remaining issues relating to the testimony of Dragan Kijac. During the testimony of Dragan Kijac on 11 and 12 November 2015, P7653 and P7662 were marked for identification pending the provision of translations. On the 16th and the 26th of November, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Prosecution by e-mail that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- must be the Defence. So I therefore correct myself. The Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence by e-mail that the relevant translations had been uploaded into e-court under doc Ids R012-5770-2-BCST and B012-6299-ET respectively and admits them into evidence, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I move to P7655, which was admitted into evidence also on the 12th of November, although there was a discussion in court about whether the document had been translated correctly. The document was admitted into evidence that same day, provided that the parties were asked to verify whether a revised English translation of the document was necessary. On the 20th of November, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence by e-mail that CLSS had verified the English translation and confirmed that it was correct. That information is hereby placed on the record. P7581 was admitted into evidence on the 19th of October. On the 12th of November, the Chamber commented that there was a discrepancy between the B/C/S original and the English translation. On 12th of February, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence that the revised English translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID V000-1274-B-ENG. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current English translation of P7581 with the new one. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. I now move to two issues relating to the testimony of Yasushi Akashi. P7694 was admitted into evidence without a B/C/S translation on the 23rd of November, 2015. On the 17th of December, the Chamber instructed the Registry to attach the B/C/S translation uploaded into e-court as doc ID R001-5622-BCST to Exhibit P7694. However, on the 18th of December, the Chamber informed the parties via e-mail that this was, in fact, incorrect and that, instead, doc ID R001-3953-BCST should be attached to the exhibit, and this change is now reflected in e-court. I'll now deal with P2508. On the 5th of February of this year, following the testimonies of witnesses Yasushi Akashi, Milos Kovic, and Milorad Dodik, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that it had added additional pages used in relation to the three aforementioned witnesses to Exhibit P2508, creating a document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02383e. The Prosecution requests that this document be assigned to Exhibit P2508 and admitted. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02383c, which is currently assigned to P2508, with document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02383e and admitted it into evidence, and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. Replacements of English translations are now following. On the 14th of November, 2013, the Chamber admitted Exhibits P2819 and P2830 into evidence. The Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence on the 23rd of February of this year advising that the revised English translations of these exhibits had been uploaded into e-court under doc IDs 0410-5762-ET and 0410-5761-ET respectively. The Chamber instructs the Registry to replace the existing English translations of P2819 and P2830 with the revised versions. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to go back to Exhibit P2508 briefly. On the record the Chamber had referred to 65 ter 02383e, and our records indicate that the proposed document was 65 ter 02382e, and we just ask that that be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, usually if new portions are added to existing exhibits, what I see is that we earlier had 2383c so one would expect as in sequence to also have then 02383e.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And my understanding is that one may also be a typographical error. If I type 02382c in to e-court, I get P2508.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll -- I'm a bit hesitant to correct it at this moment, not having been in a position to verify it, but P2508 if the parties could check, and if Mr. Registrar could also keep an eye on it, but it might be that what is to be replaced, if that's a wrong number as well, so I'd like to have it all verified and perhaps take an opportunity soon to advise the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar has verified it. And I now instruct the Registrar to replace document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02382c, which is currently assigned to P2508, with the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02382e, and admits it into evidence. And the Defence has an opportunity to revisit the matter within one week. And I noticed that Ms. Stewart, when I put that on the record, nodded in the affirmative that I had now correctly read the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to read an oral decision, a decision on the admission of Milos Kovic's expert reports. On 30th of March 2015, the Defence filed a notice of disclosure of Milos Kovic's expert reports and curriculum vitae pursuant to Rule 94 bis(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, requesting their admission into evidence. On the 24th of April, 2015, the Prosecution responded to the motion not challenging the expertise of Kovic or the relevance of the reports but seeking to cross-examine the witness as it did not accept the conclusions of the reports. On the 22nd of May of last year, the Chamber delivered its oral decision confirming the expertise of Kovic and deferring its decision on the admission of the two reports until the witness testified. Kovic testified on the 30th of November and the 1st of December, 2015, during which his curriculum vitae was admitted into evidence, and his expert reports were marked for identification as D1368 and D1369. On the 14th of January 2016 the Prosecution informed Defence and chamber, via e-mail, that it did not object to the admission of the reports with respect to the applicable law concerning expert evidence, the Chamber recalls and refers to its decision of the 19th of October, 2012 concerning expert witness Richard Butler. The Chamber notes that Kovic's expert reports analysed the conclusions of Prosecution experts Patrick Treanor and Robert Donia in relation to their respective reports on the Bosnian Serb leadership and historical events in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Kovic's reports relate to the charges set out in the indictment and are within the scope of his expertise and specialised knowledge in the area of political history. The Chamber finds, therefore, that the reports are relevant and of probative value for the purpose of their admission and, pursuant to Rule 89(C) admits D1368 and D1369 into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I move on to D649, which, on the 19th of September 2014 was marked for identification pending a discussion between the parties about a possible objection by the Prosecution. The Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber on the 11th of February of this year, stating that it did not object to its admission. The Chamber therefore admitted Exhibit D649 into evidence under seal. I now move to the remaining issues from the testimony of Mile Dosenovic, and I start with P7503 and P7500. On the 17th of August, 2015, P7503 was marked for identification pending the provision of an English translation. On the 8th of February, 2016, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that the revised English translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0425-4146-ET-3. It further noted, in relation to the translation of Exhibit P7500 - a document which contains text from document P753 - that the same revisions had been made and uploaded under doc ID 0320-8846-ET-1. On the same day, the Defence confirmed that it did not object to the revised translation, and the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the translations of P7503 and P7500 with the revised versions and admits P7503 into evidence. I move to D1196, which on 13th of August, 2015 was marked for identification and placed under seal. On the 17th of December, it was marked not admitted on the basis that the document was already in evidence as part of Exhibit D1200. On the same day, however, the Chamber noted that it would review its decision on non-admission. In the light of differences between the two documents, the Chamber hereby admitted D1196 into evidence, under seal. I now move to remaining issues from the testimony of Jose Cutileiro and Milorad Dodik, and I start with P3076. On the 8th of December, 2015, the Prosecution used excerpts of the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 2388 with witness Milorad Dodik. One excerpt from that document was already in evidence as Exhibit P3076. The Chamber allowed the Prosecution to add the additional excerpts used with the witness Dodik to the exhibit. The Prosecution uploaded a new version of the document which included these excerpts under Rule 65 ter number 2388b. On the 9th of December, the Chamber allowed additional excerpts, used with witness Cutileiro, to also be added to the exhibit. These excerpts were uploaded under Rule 65 ter number 2388c. The Chamber notes that pages 107 to 109 and 111 to 113, tendered through Milorad Dodik, have not been uploaded. The Chamber hereby instructs the Prosecution to upload a new version of the document which includes the excerpts tendered through both Dodik and Cutileiro. Once these pages are included, the Chamber will instruct the Registry to replace P3076 with that new version. I move to P7770. This exhibit was admitted into evidence on the 9th of December, 2015. On 4th of January, 2016, the Chamber e-mailed the Prosecution regarding the length of the document. On the 20th of January, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that an excerpt of the document had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 7958a. And the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace Exhibit P7770 with the proposed excerpt. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. Last item, P4582. On the 9th of December, 2015, The Prosecution noted various concerns regarding the accuracy of the English translation of Exhibit P4582. On the 27th of January, 2016, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that a revised translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0215-2880-ET2. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the existing translation of P4582 with the revised one. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter, if necessary. These were all the items I had on my agenda. Is there anything that the parties would like to raise? Nothing. Well, we'll adjourn sine die because we don't know when the Defence will be able to present further evidence. We'll hear from them not any later than by next week, Wednesday. We adjourn sine die.
